assignedReviews.card_evidence: After a tsunami, coastal communities may face destroyed homes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing types of volcanoes by activity, eruption type, and crustal location. The card discusses tsunami aftermath impacts on coastal communities, which is unrelated to volcano classification.

copy.en: After a tsunami, coastal communities may face destroyed homes, broken water and power lines, and polluted drinking water.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos ng tsunami, maaaring harapin ng mga komunidad sa baybayin ang nawasak na mga bahay, sirang linya ng tubig at kuryente, at maruming inuming tubig.
copy.bis: Human sa tsunami, ang mga komunidad sa baybayon mahimong mag-atubang sa naguba nga mga balay, naguba nga linya sa tubig ug kuryente, ug hugaw nga mainom nga tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In codominance, both alleles are expressed fully and simultaneously in the heterozygote
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that momentum depends on the mass and the velocity of a moving object that can be used to predict the impact the object will have if it hits another object
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains codominance, a genetics/inheritance concept, while G10-F-4 concerns momentum (mass and velocity of a moving object). There is no overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: In codominance, both alleles are expressed fully and simultaneously in the heterozygote, so neither trait hides the other.
copy.tl: Sa codominance, parehong alleles ay buong ipinapakita nang sabay sa heterozygote, kaya walang katangiang nagtatago sa isa pa.
copy.bis: Sa codominance, ang duha ka alleles hingpit nga gipakita sa dungan sa heterozygote, mao nga walay kinaiya nga nagtago sa lain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each codon specifies a particular amino acid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how mRNA codons specify amino acids during protein synthesis. This is molecular biology/genetics content and has no connection to soil formation from rocks and minerals, which is the subject of G5-E-4.

copy.en:
How does mRNA tell the ribosome which amino acid to add?

mRNA is read in triplet codons, groups of three bases, and each codon specifies a particular amino acid to join the growing protein chain.
copy.tl:
Paano sinasabi ng mRNA sa ribosome kung aling amino acid ang idadagdag?

Binabasa ang mRNA sa triplet codons, mga grupo ng tatlong bases, at bawat codon ay tumutukoy sa partikular na amino acid na isasali sa lumalaking protein chain.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsulti sa mRNA sa ribosome kon unsang amino acid ang idugang?

Ang mRNA basahon sa triplet codons, mga grupo sa tulo ka bases, ug matag codon nagtino sa partikular nga amino acid nga ipasulod sa nagtubo nga protein chain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each tRNA has an anticodon that pairs with a matching mRNA codon, making sure the right amino acid is added!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about tRNA anticodons and mRNA codons in protein synthesis, which is unrelated to identifying a science invention from home or the local community and explaining its everyday impact.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each tRNA has an anticodon that pairs with a matching mRNA codon, making sure the right amino acid is added!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses molecular genetics, not energy as something that causes change including light, sound, and heat energy.

copy.en:
How does tRNA know which amino acid to bring?

Each tRNA has an anticodon that pairs with a matching mRNA codon, making sure the right amino acid is added!
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng tRNA kung aling amino acid ang dadalhin?

Ang bawat tRNA ay may anticodon na nagpapares sa katugmang mRNA codon, para matiyak na tamang amino acid ang idinadagdag!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkahibalo sa tRNA kon unsang amino acid ang dad-on?

Ang matag tRNA adunay anticodon nga nagpares sa angay nga mRNA codon, aron masiguro nga husto nga amino acid ang idugang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coefficients are the numbers placed before chemical formulas in an equation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains coefficients used to balance chemical equations, a chemistry concept. G6-L-7 is about biotic and abiotic factors in an ecosystem, which is unrelated to balancing chemical equations.

copy.en: Coefficients are the numbers placed before chemical formulas in an equation, and they are used to balance the number of atoms without changing the substances themselves.
copy.tl: Ang coefficients ay ang mga numerong inilalagay bago ang chemical formula sa isang equation, at ginagamit ang mga ito para balansehin ang bilang ng mga atom nang hindi binabago ang mismong mga substance.
copy.bis: Ang coefficients mao ang mga numero nga gibutang sa atubangan sa chemical formula sa usa ka equation, ug kini gigamit aron balansehon ang gidaghanon sa mga atomo nga dili usbon ang mga substance mismo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coefficients are the big numbers written before chemical formulas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the term biotechnology and provide examples
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains coefficients in chemical equations, which is a chemistry topic. G10-L-6 is about explaining biotechnology and providing examples. There is no connection to biotechnology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coefficients are the big numbers written before chemical formulas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify examples of modern biotechnology, such as genetically modified organisms and processes (e.g. in vitro fertilization)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about chemical equation coefficients, not about modern biotechnology examples such as GMOs or in vitro fertilization. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Coefficients are the big numbers written before chemical formulas, and they tell you how many whole groups of that substance take part.
copy.tl: Ang coefficients ay ang malalaking numero na isinusulat bago ang chemical formula, at sinasabi nito kung ilang buong grupo ng substance ang kasali.
copy.bis: Ang coefficients mao ang dagkong mga numero nga gisulat sa atubangan sa chemical formula, ug kini nagsulti kung pila ka tibuok grupo sa substance ang miapil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cold-blooded animals, like snakes and lizards, don't make their own heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains thermoregulation in cold-blooded animals. It does not classify living things into groups using a table, nor does it address the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms) or similar characteristics. No direct or prerequisite support for the classification competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cold-blooded animals, like snakes and lizards, don't make their own heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about body heat sources, not about classifying Philippine animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). No drawing or diagram is used, and habitat is not mentioned. Unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Where do snakes get their body heat?

Cold-blooded animals, like snakes and lizards, don't make their own heat — they get it from their surroundings, like sunny rocks.
copy.tl:
Saan kumukuha ng init ang ahas?

Ang mga hayop na malamig ang dugo, tulad ng ahas at butiki, ay hindi gumagawa ng sariling init — kumukuha sila nito mula sa kanilang paligid.
copy.bis:
Asa mokuha og kainit ang bitin?

Ang mga hayop nga bugnaw ug dugo, sama sa bitin ug tiki, dili maghimo og kaugalingong kainit — mokuha sila niini gikan sa ilang palibot.

copy.en: Washing your hands often with soap helps keep colds and flu away.
copy.tl: Ang madalas na paghuhugas ng kamay gamit ang sabon ay nakakatulong para hindi tayo magkasipon o magka-trangkaso.
copy.bis: Ang kanunay nga paghugas sa kamot gamit ang sabon makatabang aron dili kita matakdan og sip-on o trangkaso.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the duration of a cold, not about characteristics of living things such as growing, responding, or reproducing. It does not support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A common cold usually goes away on its own in about seven days, even without medicine.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It only mentions a cold, which is a respiratory infection, but provides no information about how the respiratory system works.

copy.en: A common cold usually goes away on its own in about seven days, even without medicine.
copy.tl: Ang karaniwang sipon ay kadalasang gumagaling nang mag-isa sa loob ng pitong araw kahit walang gamot.
copy.bis: Ang sagad nga sip-on kasagaran maayo ra sa iyang kaugalingon sulod sa pito ka adlaw bisan walay tambal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Colds are an infectious disease caused by a virus
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: Card describes a viral upper respiratory infection; it provides no information about local impacts of global climate change or individual actions to reduce global warming.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Colds are an infectious disease caused by a virus
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: Card is about colds and viral infection, not evidence of global warming or climate change.

copy.en: Colds are an infectious disease caused by a virus that infects the upper respiratory system, with symptoms like sore throat, cough, mild fever, sneezing, and blocked nose.
copy.tl: Ang sipon ay nakakahawang sakit na sanhi ng virus na umaatake sa upper respiratory system, na may mga sintomas tulad ng masakit na lalamunan, ubo, bahagyang lagnat, pagbahing, at baradong ilong.
copy.bis: Ang sip-on usa ka makatakod nga sakit nga hinungdan sa virus nga moatake sa upper respiratory system, nga adunay mga sintomas sama sa sakit nga tutunlan, ubo, diyutay nga hilanat, pagbahing, ug barado nga ilong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Collaboration means working together, and many hands can clean a river or plant a garden faster than one person alone!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses teamwork and collaboration for environmental tasks; it contains no information about solutes, solvents, or solutions, so it does not support G7-M-8.

copy.en:
Why do we work with others to solve environmental problems?

Collaboration means working together, and many hands can clean a river or plant a garden faster than one person alone!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nakikipagtulungan sa iba para lutasin ang mga problema sa kapaligiran?

Ang collaboration ay ang pagtutulungan, at mas mabilis na malilinis ng maraming kamay ang isang ilog o makapagtatanim ng hardin kaysa sa isang tao lang!
copy.bis:
Ngano makigtambayayong kita sa uban aron sulbaron ang mga problema sa kinaiyahan?

Ang collaboration mao ang pagtinabangay, ug mas paspas nga malimpyohan sa daghang mga kamot ang usa ka suba o makatanom ug hardin kay sa usa ka tawo lamang!
